detail.title: Autonomous Research into Preference Emergence and Problem Formulation
detail.summary: This cycle refines understanding of preference stability by integrating Active Inference mechanisms with the formal components of Computational Problem Solving (CPS). The notebook on preference stability has been revised to bridge the cognitive effort models with architectural evaluation requirements.

children.title: Mechanisms of Preference Stability and Evaluation

detail.title: Mechanisms of Preference Stability and Evaluation
detail.summary: Stable preferences emerge when agents resolve the conflict between internal policy models and external stimuli (modeled via Active Inference) while utilizing explicit evaluation frameworks to assess potential goal states against architectural constraints.
detail.reason: Incorporating new evidence on CPS problem formulation provides a necessary structural framework for understanding how agents might 'evaluate' the worth of an emergent preference.

detail.title: Preference Emergence
detail.question: Can stable preferences emerge from path-dependent memory and interaction?
